note.p: See Ed Pope's note: Submitted by edpope on Mon, 13/08/2012 - 20:19 27.2.1795 at Frend's. Supposed by Ben Ross Schneider, "Wordsworth's Cambridge Education", and Kenneth Johnston "The Hidden Wordsworth" to be Thomas Edwards DNB 1759-1842, son of Rev Thomas Edwards PCC 1785, which is likely; but various writers have confused him with Rev John Edwards of Birmingham and stated that he helped Coleridge with the Watchman in 1796; and the DNB, following Alum Cantab, confuses him with another Thomas Edwards (Alum Ox) who was vicar of Aldford Cheshire for many years and died 1842. He was curate of Swavesey, Cambs and The Bury and Norwich Post of 5.4.1820 records his death at Huntingdon on his way to Leamington Spa. In 1796 he sold his library. He was also featured in Literary Memoirs of Living Authors p173. If this entry was him there is no reason to think he was any of the other Edwards entries in Godwin's diary
